note: Vol. I No. 36. THE COUNTY ELECTION IS THE NEWS and it is the only news: page 3 column 1 gives the vote of the four precincts of Cook county and the slate that stood in them, cut down its left edge so that nearly every forename has to be supplied from the fuller printing of 1834-08-13. THE MONTH'S ONLY POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST IS IN THIS ISSUE AND IS NOT CHICAGO'S — the Hennepin return of 1 July, in its fifth week, cut across two segmenter columns (claims c010 and c011); the Chicago list has been withdrawn since 1834-07-23 and does not return in August. Pages 1 and 2 are advertising and national reprint; the town is on page 1 column 3 (the real-estate column, five numbered lots), page 3 columns 4-6 and page 4. Page 3 columns 3 and page 4 columns 1-4 are the Tesseract fallback and are cut down one edge; every supply below is bracketed.

claims.notes: THE COUNTY'S FIRST GENERAL ELECTION UNDER THE NEW TOWN, and the paper says plainly what it could and could not report: the vote of the four precincts of this county only, because nothing had come in from the rest of the state. THE COLUMN IS CUT DOWN ITS LEFT EDGE by the leading article, so nearly every name survives without its forename ('W. Sherman', 'des Kinzie', 'plen M. Salsburg') and the vote figures survive better than the offices they belong to. EVERY FORENAME SUPPLIED HERE IS READ OFF THE ISSUE OF 1834-08-13, page 2 column 5, lines 2010-2037, where the same slate is printed whole — 'Silas W. Sherinan', 'Russel E. Heacock', 'George W. Snow', 'John Shrigley', 'dward E. Hunter', 'Isaac Scarret', 'James Kinzie', 'Stephen M. Balsbury'. That is a supply from another printing of the same list, and it is bracketed as one. THE CANAL IS THE STATED TEST for the Assembly candidates — 'supported entirely with respect to their known [views] in favor of the Illinois and Michigan Ca[nal]' — which is the town's own account of what it was voting on in 1834.

claims.notes: A SCHEDULED PACKET ACROSS THE LAKE, ADVERTISED AS A SERVICE RATHER THAN AS A VOYAGE. claims.notes: FIRE INSURANCE IS ON OFFER IN CHICAGO IN 1834, and the agency is a New York company's — the Howard, of the city of New-York — placed through the town's largest forwarding house. claims.notes: THE FOURTH WEEKLY PRICES CURRENT IN THIS CORPUS and the first of the August run, signed the same way as July's: reported for the Democrat by P. F. Peck, the merchant at LaSalle and South Water (1834-07-02, claim c023 there). THE FIGURES ARE ALMOST ENTIRELY GONE from this printing — the segmenter cut the table down its figure edge, so the commodity NAMES survive and their prices do not, which is the exact reverse of the cut on 1834-07-23 (claim c001 there, where the figures survived and the names did not). Nothing is supplied across that gap: a price this file cannot read is left as an ellipsis rather than carried over from another week, because a prices current that is copied from the week before is not a prices current. WHAT THE TABLE IS FOR HERE is its SHAPE — Flour and Meal, Grain, Provisions, Groceries, Domestics, Iron, Materials, Exchange — and the Materials section is the one this project reads: square timber priced by the thousand, shingles, lime, stone and wood, which is the 1834 cost of building the town.

claims.normalized: List of Let[ters remaining] IN the Post Offi[c]e at [Hennepin, Ill. on the 1]st day of July[, 1834] […] David Austin […] [uncertain: Jota Baroma] […] Robert Barms 2 […] Gaylord Hayes […] [uncertain: Jobn Knoz] […] THOS. GALA[HER, Jr. P. M.]
claims.notes: THE ONLY POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST STANDING ANYWHERE IN AUGUST 1834, AND IT IS NOT CHICAGO'S. It is the Hennepin return of 1 July 1834, signed THOS. GALAHER, Jr. P. M., in its fifth week of standing — the same list the issue of 1834-07-30 carries at page 3 column 4, lines 3710-3771. THE TWO PRINTINGS CUT IT IN DIFFERENT PLACES, which is why both are needed: 1834-07-30 gives the names from L onward (Amos Leonard, Levi Lucas, Henry F. Miller, Charles Knock, Daniel Newton, Jerry Parsons, Joseph Ross, John Reed, Rev. Wm. Royal, and six more) and this printing gives the head of the alphabet, A to K, which that one lost. THIS CLAIM IS THE A-K HALF, in segmenter column 2; claim c011 is the L-W tail, in column 3. THE LIST IS WOVEN LINE BY LINE with David Carver's lumber advertisement, so `lines_of_claim` names only the nine lines that carry the list and the other twenty-three in the range belong to Carver. RULING 1 IS SATISFIED AT ARM'S LENGTH: a listed name mints a resident candidate, and every name here is a candidate resident of HENNEPIN, a hundred miles down the Illinois, not of this town — `associated_places` says so on each one so that no later pass can read them as Chicago people.

Royal' at 3747, '[uncertain: Aaron Willaace s]' at 3757, '[uncertain: Alone Wood]' at 3767 — a supply from another printing of the same list, bracketed as one, and never quietly merged into the quote. THE HAND COUNT, which is the acceptance clause of T-0290: the printed Hennepin list of 1 July 1834 carries EIGHTEEN addressee entries where the two printings can be read together — five here in the A-K half (Austin, Baroma, Barms, Hayes, Knox), six here in the L-W half (L. P. Miller, Miller, Ross, Royal, Whittaker, Wallace, Wood is seven), and the 1834-07-30 printing's own L-onward run adds Leonard, Lucas, Henry F. Miller, W. L. May, Knock, Newton, Parsons, Reed, Screech, Tracy, Thompson and Watson. COUNTED STRICTLY OFF THE LINES THIS ISSUE CARRIES, and that is what this claim asserts: eleven names in the two columns of 1834-08-06, plus the postmaster. The union with the other printing is stated in the note and is not minted here, because a claim is made from its own lines.

Section 16 of every township was the school section, and Chicago's was sold off from 1833 — so 'Block 120, in the School Section' is a claim about the town's edge rather than about its centre, and the same seller's advertisement stands unchanged through the month (1834-08-13 line 2949, 1834-08-20 line 3226). The line 'GULACHARD, / Bonse and Land dgent' immediately below belongs to a DIFFERENT advertisement woven into this column and is excluded from the claim.

claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. The display line at 320 is transcribed '[uncertain: GULACHARD,]' — the transcription's own uncertainty mark, kept as it stands. It is consistent with the surname T-0408 read off the two non-fallback columns and it is NOT read as a witness to it here; nothing is supplied from it and no forename appears. THE PROPRIETOR'S NAME IS NOT READ HERE and none is supplied into the quote: the record's ‘W. G. Blanchard’ stands on T-0408's reading of the two impressions whose columns are NOT Tesseract fallbacks (1834-07-16 line 5527, 1834-09-17 line 3292) and on identity.json's declared firm merge, not on this impression. THE CARD IS SET OUT OF ORDER in this column: the address (324) stands above '1 Houses to Let.' (325) and '1001 section.' (326), which is 'School section.' The normalization puts them back in the card's order; the quote does not.
